changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For buyers replacing a homegrown billing system, do not lead with revenue growth. Lead with roadmap time recovered, in the buyer's words: stop billing being "a tax on the roadmap". Use the demo moment as proof: a pricing change that used to take a quarter is done in minutes ("a quarter of roadmap in five minutes"). Then put a cost on that time.
changes.why: The rep's revenue-growth framing was rejected outright ("we're not trying to grow revenue with billing"), while the demo landed because it recovered roadmap time that a quarter-long pricing change was eating.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When a champion asks for payback or anything for finance, do not answer with the generic economic impact study. Offer instead: "Let's build your number together this week", meaning a payback figure built from the customer's own inputs that the champion can take to the CFO.
changes.why: The generic ROI deck with the study was sent in answer to the payback request, and the champion said plainly he could not get the deal past the CFO without "a number that's ours"; the session to build that number had still not happened when the freeze came.

changes.change: Add a cost-of-homegrown-billing proof point for status-quo deals. Price the status quo from the buyer's own inputs: engineering time spent on pricing changes, billing errors, and subscriptions that lapse because failed card payments are never chased. Pair the involuntary-churn line with M10 (smart retries) as a recoverable loss, not revenue growth. Purpose: turn "a nice to have" into something finance treats as "on fire".
changes.why: The rep named their own number (engineering time, billing errors) as the missing proof, the champion had mentioned lapsed subscriptions from failed cards that no one added up, and finance dismissed the project as a nice to have because nothing was on fire.

changes.change: For buyers with existing card-on-file subscriptions, add a migration proof point: a reference customer the buyer can talk to who moved existing subscriptions without asking their customers for card details again, and in stages. Offer the reference call, not just a document.
changes.why: The champion's migration concerns were no re-collection of card details and a staged move, and when offered a doc he asked to talk to someone who had done it.
